Last September when Apple launched the iPhone 17, the countdown began for the company's new flagship to break a 15-year-old record. The record will take over a year to surpass, but according to current rumours, the iPhone 17 will be the first model to take the crown.

The iPhone 4 had an unusually long sales cycle

That record belongs to the iPhone 4, which went on sale in June 2010 and remained Apple's top iPhone until October 2011. Because Apple shifted its flagship launch cycle from summer to autumn that year, the iPhone 4 held the title for nearly 16 months.

For consumers who were planning to "wait for the iPhone 5," this was a particularly frustrating period. Apple eventually released the iPhone 4S, which looked almost identical to the iPhone 4 on the outside; all the changes were internal: the debut of Siri, an upgraded camera, and improved performance.

Strictly speaking, the iPhone 4's launch also went through several stages. In the United States, AT&T was the exclusive carrier and launched it first. Half a year later, Verizon became the second US carrier. Ten months later, the long-delayed white model finally arrived.

Since then, no iPhone has been able to replicate the iPhone 4's 15-month flagship sales cycle. The closest was the iPhone 11 Pro, which held the position for 13 months because the iPhone 12 was delayed due to the pandemic. Other special cases include the gap of more than four years between the iPhone SE and the iPhone SE 2, and then the iPhone 16e, but these were intentional arrangements, not flagship cycles.

The iPhone 17 is expected to break the record (but the situation is different)

The iPhone 18 is not expected to arrive until spring 2027, meaning the iPhone 17 will remain at the top of Apple's mainstream flagship lineup for about 18 months, surpassing the iPhone 4's record and setting a new record for the longest sales cycle of a standard iPhone.

Model Launch Replaced by Duration at top iPhone 17 September 2025 iPhone 18, Spring 2027 (expected) ~550 days, ~18 months (projected) iPhone 4 iPhone 4S 477 days, ~15.7 months iPhone 11 Pro iPhone 12 Pro 399 days, ~13.1 months iPhone (2007) iPhone 3G 378 days, ~12.4 months

The biggest difference between the iPhone 4 era and today is the arrival of the Pro series. The long wait from the iPhone 4 to the iPhone 4S left consumers hoping for new surprises experiencing a severe upgrade drought.

The most upvoted comment was posted by Rex Videos

I think this depends on how you define "flagship"

During the cycle from the iPhone 17 to the iPhone 18, the Pro models will still be updated annually, and Apple's first foldable iPhone is also expected to launch simultaneously.

The foldable phone will be the biggest hardware change in iPhone history, but the iPhone 17 is still expected to break the record for the longest sales cycle between standard flagship models.

The shortest iPhone cycle

Incidentally, the shortest gap between iPhone upgrade cycles might surprise you. The cycle from the iPhone 12 to the iPhone 13 lasted only 11 months, as Apple adjusted its pace after pandemic-related delays.

However, although the iPhone X was announced in September 2017, it did not actually go on sale until November of the same year, meaning it was replaced by the iPhone XS just 10 months later.
